title: CISA: critical flaws in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1 and ELBC2000 trailer brake controllers
summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-323-02 lists three flaws in Elecbrakes products used in Australia and New Zealand: an unprotected firmware-update channel, replayable commands, and unauthenticated command injection over Bluetooth LE. Two are rated CVSS v3.1 9.6. CISA says no public exploitation has been reported to it. Fixes exist for EB2 and VM1; none for the discontinued ELBC2000.
plain: Three security flaws in Australian-made vehicle brake controllers could let a nearby attacker send commands. Two models have fixes; an older one does not.
exec: Transport operators using these controllers face remote-control risk with no fix for the oldest model.
action: Update EB2 to firmware 3.0.4.4.3 and VM1 to 1.3.4.2.1 via the Elecbrakes app; replace or isolate ELBC2000 units.

review.note: Re-read CISA ICSA-26-323-02: three CVE ids, two CVSS 3.1 9.6 and one 6.1, fixed EB2 3.0.4.4.3 and VM1 1.3.4.2.1, ELBC2000 no fix, no public exploitation reported to CISA, AU/NZ, date 2026-11-19 all match; severity 2 and confirmed status fit
